title: Microsoft Teams: report suspicious guest invitations to your admin
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout facts, reporting controls, default setting and administrator roles are supported. It distinguishes the documented reporting settings from guest-invitation details and licensing that Microsoft has not yet published.

claims.claim: Microsoft Teams plans to let users report suspicious guest invitations to their IT admin for review.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams will enable users to report suspicious guest invitations directly from Teams. When users receive an unexpected or potentially malicious guest invitation, they can report it to their IT admin for review

claims.claim: The invitations concerned invite the recipient to join another organisation as a guest.
claims.quote: When users receive an unexpected or potentially malicious invitation to join another organization as a guest, they can report it to their IT admin for review

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationales
claims.claim: Users initiate a report when declining a suspicious guest invitation in Teams.
claims.quote: Users can report suspicious guest invitations when declining them in Teams.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Guest-invitation reports reach the IT admin through the User reported security submissions report in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Reports are shared with their IT admin through the User reported security submissions report in the Teams admin center

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Guest-invitation reports are also shared with Microsoft for review.
claims.quote: Reports are shared with their IT admin through the User reported security submissions report in the Teams admin center and with Microsoft for review.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe guest-invitation reporting itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest invitations" "report". Opened Microsoft Learn end-user-reporting-security, end-user-reported-security-signal and defender-office-365/submissions-teams; none describes reporting invitations to join another organisation as a guest.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing Teams security reporting supports chat and channel messages.
claims.quote: Users can report messages in Teams from chats and channels for security concern and for incorrect detection.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Users can report suspicious external users while blocking them in Teams.
claims.quote: User can report suspicious external users while blocking them in Teams, from external chat requests and user profile cards.

claims.where: summary; controls[0]; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing Report a security concern messaging-policy setting governs guest-invitation reporting.
claims.quote: The capability is controlled through the Teams messaging policy setting for Report a security concern.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The governing Teams admin center setting is on by default, so the feature can arrive without new admin action.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center: 'On' by default and controls whether users are able to report messages and user from Teams.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning off the shared Report a security concern policy removes the reporting option for affected users.
claims.quote: Admins can manage this capability through Teams admin center > Messaging policies > Report a security concern.

claims.claim: The existing User report category includes the reporter's name.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn has not documented the contents of a guest-invitation report.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest invitation" reporting automatic action notification report contains outcome. Opened end-user-reported-security-signal, end-user-reporting-security and submissions-teams; none specifies guest-invitation report fields.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity, Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automatic invitation remediation triggered by reporting, and the notice describes no autonomous action.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest invitation" reporting notification automatic remediation. Read MC1530615, end-user-reporting-security, end-user-reported-security-signal and submissions-teams; no automatic action on a reported guest invitation is described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The effect of reporting on an associated guest account in the inviting organisation is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams report suspicious guest invitations licensing price default notification automatic remediation guest account reporting. Read MC1530615 and the three cited reporting pages; none describes an effect on an associated guest account.

claims.claim: Invitation-specific notification and alert behaviour is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest invitation" reporting notification automatic remediation. Opened end-user-reporting-security, end-user-reported-security-signal and submissions-teams; no invitation-specific alert or notification behaviour is stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the outcome for the reporter or what Microsoft does after receiving a guest-invitation report.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest invitation" reporting automatic action notification report contains outcome. Read MC1530615 and the cited reporting pages; no guest-invitation-specific follow-up or outcome for the reporter is described.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The guest-invitation reporting licensing model, price and meter are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest invitation" "report" "licensing"; "Teams" "guest invitations" report price meter licence. Read MC1530615, both Teams reporting pages, messaging-policies-in-teams and submissions-teams; none specifies guest-invitation licensing or charges.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: MC1530615 names no licence requirement or charge.
claims.quote: No action is required for organizations that already have Report a security concern enabled in their Teams messaging policy. Admins can manage this capability through Teams admin center > Messaging policies > Report a security concern.

claims.claim: The User reported security submissions report page lists reporting settings as prerequisites and names no licence in them.
claims.quote: Reported interactions appear in the User reported security submissions reports only after users submit reports. ... Users can submit reports only when the required reporting settings are enabled in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The Teams security-reporting and messaging-policy pages specify Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Defender XDR for malicious-message reporting.
claims.quote: Report a security concern - When this is ON, users can report malicious messages in Microsoft Teams in organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR.

claims.claim: The Defender reporting page specifies Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Defender XDR, including for message reporting.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report messages, calls, meetings, or meeting participants in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Custom messaging policies can be assigned to users, allowing reporting settings to differ by assigned policy.
claims.quote: Users in your organization will automatically get the global policy, unless you create and assign a custom policy. Edit the settings in the global policy or create and assign one or more custom policies to turn on or turn off the features that you want.

claims.claim: The notice requires no action from organisations with Report a security concern already enabled.
claims.quote: No action is required for organizations that already have Report a security concern enabled in their Teams messaging policy.

claims.claim: Learn says user reporting of external users is not yet supported in Microsoft Defender.
claims.quote: User reporting of external users is not yet supported in Microsoft Defender.

claims.where: Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not address whether guest-invitation reports are supported in Defender.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest invitations" "report" "setting". Opened end-user-reporting-security and defender-office-365/submissions-teams, including its reporting configuration; neither addresses guest-invitation reports in Defender.

claims.claim: The cited page documents Teams admin center > Messaging policies > policy > Report a security concern.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams Admin Center ... In the left navigation, select Messaging policies. ... Select a policy. ... Turn on the setting: Report a security concern.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell documents Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity <policy> -AllowSecurityEndUserReporting $true for the general reporting setting, with feature applicability explicitly caveated.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy ... [[-Identity] <XdsIdentity>] ... [-AllowSecurityEndUserReporting <Boolean>] ... This setting determines if users can report any security concern posted in message to their admin. Possible values: True, False

claims.claim: The Teams reporting page points to Settings & policies for the new admin experience.
claims.quote: To access this policy in the new experience, go to Settings & policies.

claims.claim: AllowSecurityEndUserReporting is Boolean and accepts False to disable reporting.
claims.quote: This setting determines if users can report any security concern posted in message to their admin. Possible values: True, False ... Type: | Boolean

claims.claim: The report is under Teams admin center > Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > User reported security submissions.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports. ... On the View reports tab, under Report, select User reported security submissions.

claims.claim: The documented report categories are Calling, Chats and channels, and User, with no guest-invitation category listed.
claims.quote: Under Report category, choose one of the following categories: ... Calling ... Chats and channels ... User

claims.claim: No API for the Teams admin center User reported security submissions report is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "User reported security submissions" "API" "PowerShell"; "User reported security submissions" report API site:learn.microsoft.com/graph. Read the report page and Graph reportSubmission/userReport excerpts; none documents an API for this report.

claims.claim: No guest-invitation reporting switch separate from Report a security concern is documented on the UI or API surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest invitations" "report" "setting"; "guest invitations" "report" site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams. Read MC1530615 and Teams reporting and messaging-policy references; no separate switch is documented.

claims.claim: The Defender-side reporting setting must also be on for user-reported messages to appear on its Submissions page.
claims.quote: If "Report a security concern" is turned on in the Teams admin center, it also needs to be turned on in the Defender portal for user reported messages to show up correctly on the User reported tab on the Submissions page.

claims.claim: Learn has not explicitly confirmed that AllowSecurityEndUserReporting covers guest-invitation reporting.
claims.quote: Searched: "guest invitations" "report" site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams. Opened Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy and read AllowSecurityEndUserReporting, Identity and syntax; its description covers concerns posted in messages, not guest invitations.

claims.claim: Microsoft names Teams Administrator or Global Administrator for configuring user reporting in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To view or configure user reporting in the Teams admin center, you need to be a member of the Global Administrator or Teams Administrator roles.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents that Teams Administrators can access all reports in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Teams Administrator ... Access all reports in the Microsoft Teams admin center
